title: Usage Insights: query API endpoints (breakdown + top drivers) with pagination + caching
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
Goal
Implement backend query endpoints powering the Console Usage Insights views:
1) Route + model cost/usage breakdown tables
2) “Top cost drivers” + “What changed?” insights cards

This ticket covers:
- API endpoints (request/response semantics, filter validation)
- Pagination strategy (cursor-based)
- Caching strategy (server-side + cache headers)
- Guardrails for query complexity (time ranges, dimensions)

Non-goals
- Warehouse aggregation jobs/schema (ENG-3812)
- Route normalization library (ENG-3813)
- UI implementation (ENG-3815)
- CSV export job lifecycle (ENG-3816)

Background / context
Customers (and internal Finance) need consistent, drillable cost attribution by API route and model, with totals reconciling against billing. The Console requires interactive queries (p95 latency targets) and stable pagination, while also handling late-arriving telemetry and freshness indicators.

References
- Confluence API contract: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/usage-insights-api-contract.json
- Query service system doc: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/usage-insights-query-service.json
- ADR: route normalization & attribution: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-route-normalization-and-attribution.json
- SLO budget (beta): sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/usage-insights-slo-and-performance-budget.json

Proposed endpoints (v1)
All endpoints require auth and workspace context. RBAC gating will be enforced in ENG-3820 (this ticket wires permission checks but may feature-flag the response fields until ENG-3820 merges).

1) Breakdown query
GET /v1/usage/insights/breakdown
Purpose: Populate the Route × Model breakdown table and drilldown views.

Required query params
- workspace_id (from auth context; not a raw query param in Console calls)
- start, end (ISO-8601 timestamps; inclusive start, exclusive end)

Optional query params
- project_id
- environment (prod|staging|dev; if present)
- deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)
- region
- route (canonical normalized route string; see ENG-3813)
- model (stable model ID; version bucketing handled in ENG-3823)
- group_by (comma-separated list; allowed: route, model, project, environment, deployment_mode, region)
- sort (allowed: cost_usd, tokens_in, tokens_out, requests, p95_latency_ms)
- order (asc|desc)
- limit (default 50, max 200)
- cursor (opaque)

Response fields (per row)
- dimensions: route, model, project_id, environment, deployment_mode, region (only those in group_by)
- metrics: cost_usd, requests, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit_rate, retries, fallbacks, streaming_requests, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms
- computed hints: context_length_p50, context_length_p95 (if available; otherwise omitted)
- freshness: dataset_max_timestamp, aggregation_lag_seconds (returned at top-level in response)

2) Top drivers
GET /v1/usage/insights/top-drivers
Purpose: Returns ranked explanations of cost drivers and deltas vs previous period.

Query params
- start, end
- compare (optional; default “previous_period”)
- filters: project_id, environment, route, model, deployment_mode, region
- limit (default 10, max 25)

Response
- drivers[]: { driver_key, title, impact_usd, impact_percent, explanation, recommended_actions[], supporting_metrics }
- changes[] (optional): { dimension, before, after, delta_percent, explanation }
- freshness block (same shape as breakdown)

Notes on “driver_key”
Keep stable keys for UI + telemetry: token_out_increase, cache_hit_drop, retries_increase, fallback_rate_increase, context_length_shift, model_mix_shift, streaming_overhead_increase.

Pagination
- Cursor-based pagination for breakdown rows. Cursor encodes sort + last_seen tuple (dimension values + metric used for sort) and is signed to prevent tampering.
- Cursor invalidation: If underlying aggregation version changes (schema bump) return 400 with error code INSIGHTS_CURSOR_INVALID and message “Cursor expired; rerun query.”

Caching strategy
Primary goal is to keep p95 interactive queries < 700ms for common ranges (24h/7d) and protect the warehouse from identical repeated queries from Console refreshes and multiple viewers.

Layer 1: Service cache
- Cache key: (workspace_id, endpoint, normalized filters, start/end bucketed to minute, group_by, sort, order, limit, cursor)
- TTLs:
  - last 24h: 60s
  - 7d: 5m
  - 30d: 15m (but may be blocked by guardrails; see below)
- Store: Redis in the console-backend cluster
- Compression: enable for payloads > 64KB

Layer 2: HTTP semantics
- Set Cache-Control: private, max-age=30 (Console only; do not allow shared caches)
- ETag on full response bodies; support If-None-Match to reduce payload

Guardrails / limits
- Hard max time range in beta: 31 days. For > 31 days return 400 with error code INSIGHTS_RANGE_TOO_LARGE.
- If group_by includes > 3 dimensions, return 400 INSIGHTS_TOO_MANY_DIMENSIONS.
- If route filter is unnormalized (contains raw UUID segments) return 400 INSIGHTS_ROUTE_NOT_CANONICAL, with message instructing to use normalized routes.
- If query is likely to exceed row limit due to cardinality (estimated via preflight stats), return 422 INSIGHTS_QUERY_TOO_EXPENSIVE with a hint to add filters (project/model/route) or reduce time range.

Auth / permissions
- Endpoint access is feature-flagged for beta allowlist (ENG-3825).
- Cost fields gated behind “view_cost” permission; if user lacks permission:
  - Return 403 for /top-drivers (since it’s inherently cost)
  - For /breakdown either (a) return 403 or (b) return rows with cost_usd omitted and a “cost_hidden=true” marker. Decision: return 403 to avoid “partial confusing” UI states. (Design and PM aligned in Slack #eng-platform 1737821108.)
- All access logged (audit log events added in ENG-3820/ENG-3816 for exports; this ticket ensures request IDs and principal IDs propagate).

Acceptance criteria
- Endpoints implemented behind feature flag and wired to aggregated dataset (ENG-3812).
- Cursor pagination works consistently with sorting by cost_usd and tokens_out; verified via integration tests.
- Caching reduces repeat identical query warehouse hits by >80% in staging load test.
- Error responses follow API standards with stable error codes and actionable messages.
- p95 latency for 7d breakdown (group_by=route,model) < 700ms in staging with warm cache; < 1500ms cold.

Implementation notes
- Query compilation: translate filters to warehouse predicates only on partitioned fields (time_bucket, workspace_id, project_id) where possible.
- All time handling in UTC; Console passes user-local but must convert. Response includes start/end echoed back in UTC.
- For “previous_period” comparisons, compute compare_start = start - (end-start), compare_end = start.

Testing
- Unit tests: validation (range, group_by), cursor encode/decode, error codes
- Integration tests: seeded dataset fixtures for pagination stability and sorting
- Load test: 20 concurrent users, 1 rps each, mix of 24h and 7d queries; verify cache hit rate

Rollout plan
- Deploy endpoints disabled by default.
- Enable for internal dogfood workspaces, then beta allowlist (ENG-3825).
- Monitor warehouse query volume + cache hit metrics; coordinate with SRE on alert thresholds.

Open questions
1) Should /breakdown support returning both “totals” and “rows” in one call?
   - Decision: yes. Top-level totals included to keep UI totals consistent with table rows.
2) Should /top-drivers require a compare param always?
   - Decision: default compare=previous_period; UI can override.
3) How to handle missing route tags (partial data)?
   - Decision: return freshness + partial_data=true when ingestion gaps detected (from data quality signals). UI will show banner (ENG-3824).
